findings.title: Test file exports helpers that nothing imports
findings.description: The test file marks `designPath`, `tasksPath`, `completeBeta`, `worktreeCtx`, `createRoutedSetup`, `dryRun`, `aboutSubject` and the `RoutedSetup` interface as `export`. A repo-wide grep for `routedFixes.test` found no importer. Exporting from a `*.test.ts` file is also risky because importing it re-registers its `describe` blocks. Either drop the `export` keywords or move the helpers to `tests/helpers/`, where `gitWorktreeFixture.ts` already lives.

findings.title: CLI and MCP tests import a fixture from another package's tests directory
findings.description: `packages/cli/tests/commands/check-worktree-fix.test.ts` and `packages/mcp-server/tests/workflowCheckRouting.test.ts` import `../../../core/tests/helpers/gitWorktreeFixture.js`. The fixture is not part of core's public surface, and the relative path breaks if the package layout changes. Share it through a test-support package or a dev-only export instead.

findings.title: Single-slice fix path has no coverage in the mocked CLI check tests
findings.description: `check.test.ts` still declares `mockFix` and `mockFixAll`, and the `ConsistencyChecker` mock still returns them. The new code never calls `checker.fix` or `checker.fixAll`: fix mode now runs `check` or `checkAll`, then `planRoutedFixes`, then `applyFixes`. The mocks are dead, and any remaining assertions on them check behaviour the code no longer has. A grep shows `packages/cli/tests/commands/check.test.ts:311` still has a comment about "NOT fixAll". Remove the stale mocks and assertions. The behaviour is covered by the real-git integration tests, but the mocked suite should not imply otherwise.

findings.title: `fixAction!` non-null assertions rely on filtering done elsewhere
findings.description: `fixRelPath` and `routeView` use `finding.fixAction!`. Today every caller pre-filters with `f.fixable && f.fixAction`. That invariant is not encoded in the type, so a future caller of the exported `fixRelPath` or `gateByReadiness` could crash at runtime. Make `fixRelPath` take a finding type with `fixAction` required, or throw an explicit error when it is missing. The TypeScript rules also discourage assertions without a documented reason.

findings.title: Fix-mode check and confirm flow is duplicated between CLI and MCP
findings.description: Both `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts` and `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/workflowTools.ts` build `scopeViews` and `runCheck` with the same slice-narrowing logic. Both also resolve the invoking checkout and call `planRoutedFixes` then `applyFixPlan`. The project's DRY rule says to extract this into one core helper. The CLI and MCP paths can drift, for example in how errors are mapped (`UserError` in the CLI, `errorResult` in MCP).

findings.title: Display-layer coupling to `showWorktree`
findings.description: `printCheckOutput` picks the routed report with `fixRes && showWorktree`. That flag means "show worktree prefixes", not "multi-checkout fix". The two currently coincide. If the display flag is ever decoupled from the number of checkouts, this branch will pick the wrong report. A comment, or a check on `fixRes.commits` and `fixRes.deferred`, would make the intent explicit.

findings.title: Failed-restore case leaves `fixed` counting uncommitted writes
findings.description: When the commit fails and the restore also fails, the log entries and `fixed` stay, and `fixErrors` carries the message. This is deliberate and covered by test 7. The failures are also logged with `console.error` in a library module. This is acceptable, but a structured logger would be better if one exists in core.
